decisions.reason: The cited deterministic linear-Gaussian definition requires d_t and p_t to be positive integers. The assigned Definition did not exclude zero dimensions, so its assertion that every frozen path meets those hypotheses was unsupported. Added exactly those dimension requirements; singular state and process covariances remain allowed.

The unqualified target t allowed t=T+1, while s=min(t+L,T)=T then yields a path with no time-t coordinate. Made the algorithm domain explicit: integer lag L>=0 and t in {0,...,T}. The proof now checks t<=s<=T before taking the coordinate projection.

F1 defines a smoothing law on the whole state path, so the claimed full smoothing law delta_b had the wrong state space and could not be compared directly to Bernoulli(1/2) on X_0. The full path law is delta_(b,b,b); its time-0 marginal is delta_b. Corrected the Example and verification to compare time-0 marginals throughout.

reviews.reason: Checked the complete Definition against def-linear-gaussian-state-space-model-with-independent-noises: fixed-path coefficient dimensions, independent Gaussian noises and semidefinite state covariances agree, with positive observation covariance ensuring innovation invertibility. Explicit positive integer dimensions now meet the supplier domain. AC and conditional-version qualifications are preserved.

Checked the exact fixed-lag algorithm and complete backward-factorization proof. At each admissible prefix horizon s the supplied exact kernels generate the conditional path law; because 0<=t<=s, its time-t projection has the claimed conditional marginal. The full-measure, conditional-version, T=0 and L=0 qualifications remain valid. No new convergence claim or AC use is introduced. Also corrected the contract boundary note to use the actual full-measure factorization assumption.

Checked the entire finite model: both Y_2 outcomes have probability 1/2, Y_1 is constant, the full path equals (b,b,b) conditional on Y_2=b, and projection gives the time-0 law delta_b. Enumerating subsets of {0,1} gives total variation 1/2 from the lagged Bernoulli law. The repaired theorem applies with t=0,L=1,T=2; deterministic kernels satisfy the factorization assumptions. Updated its exact F4 supplier quotation and synchronized its derivation rows.
